items.title: Revived: Auto-Seed Work on Idle Detection (cycle #356)
items.raw_description: Implement the idle detection auto-seed mechanism after 30+ consecutive idle cycles. The system needs a post-cycle hook that detects fully idle state and automatically revives archived ideas or generates new maintenance tasks. This implements what the Self-Healing Idle Detection System proposed. Current state: 31+ consecutive idle cycles detected, 74 ideas archived, 200 tasks done, 80 projects done, 103 pipelines done.
items.refined_description: Phase 1: Build a post-cycle hook that detects fully idle state (no pending tasks, no active pipelines, no active projects). Phase 3: Integrate with the evolution system to track idle patterns as failure records. Phase 4: Prevent duplicate revival of already-done ideas. Implementation: Python module in src/ai_embedded_company/orchestrator/ with CLI entry point.

items.raw_description: When cycle detects fully idle state, auto-seed new ideas from archived ones or known improvement opportunities
items.refined_description: Design and implement an auto-seed mechanism that detects fully idle autonomous cycle states (no pending tasks, no active pipelines, all projects completed) and proactively generates seed ideas from: (1) archived ideas with highest revival priority scored by relevance to current system gaps, (2) known system improvement opportunities detected via pattern analysis of cycle logs, (3) periodic maintenance tasks (database health, test coverage, dependency updates). Deliverables: idle state detection module, idea revival priority scorer, auto-generation cron trigger that fires after 3+ consecutive idle cycles. Phase 1: Implement idle state detection with consecutive cycle tracking. Phase 2: Build revival scoring heuristic for archived ideas. Phase 3: Auto-seed generation and API integration. Phase 4: Test the full idle-detection-to-seed pipeline. Pure software — no hardware required.

items.title: Revived: Implement Top Evolution Antibodies as Code Changes (auto-seeded cycle #326)
items.raw_description: The evolution system has identified 8 failure patterns with approved antibody candidates. This initiative implements the top 3 antibodies as actual code changes: (1) Add a guard on project completion that verifies all associated tasks are done before marking completed, (2) Auto-advance pipeline phases after creation so pipelines are not left in todo phases, (3) Require refined_description on ideas before allowing pipeline start. These changes harden the pipeline lifecycle against the most frequent failure patterns detected across 49 pipelines.
items.refined_description:
Implement the top 3 approved evolution antibody candidates as concrete Python code changes.

Phase 1: Project completion guard — modify project PATCH endpoint to verify all associated tasks are done before allowing completion, returning 409 Conflict if orphan tasks exist.

Phase 2: Pipeline auto-advance — modify pipeline creation to auto-call advance through initial phases so pipelines do not sit in todo phases after creation.

Phase 3: Idea refinement gate — before starting a pipeline from an idea, require refined_description to be non-null; return 400 if missing.

All phases include pytest tests verifying the new behavior. Pure software maintenance — no hardware required.

items.title: Revived: Pipeline-Type Matching Improvement (auto-seeded cycle #325)
items.raw_description: Cycle #261 identified that the pipeline-type keyword matcher chose "web-fullstack" over "quick-prototype" for a pure backend change because tags contained "evolution" and "self-improvement". The heuristic keyword matching system needs improvement: (1) Audit the keyword-to-pipeline mapping for false matches, (2) Add negative keywords / exclusion rules, (3) Add tie-breaking logic that prefers narrower matches, (4) Add fallback override when only backend code is changed. Fix the template system to select appropriate pipeline types for non-hardware, non-research, pure-backend ideas.
items.refined_description: Fix the pipeline-type heuristic keyword matching system that selects inappropriate pipeline templates for non-hardware, non-research ideas. Phase 1: Audit all keyword-to-pipeline_type mappings in the pipeline template system, identifying false matches where tags trigger wrong pipeline types. Phase 2: Add negative keyword / exclusion rules to prevent false matches (e.g., presence of C/C++ code context selects embedded-firmware, absence of MCU keywords excludes it). Phase 3: Add tie-breaking logic preferring narrower matches over broader ones when multiple pipeline types score equally. Phase 4: Add fallback override selecting quick-prototype when only backend Python code is detected (no frontend framework imports, no MCU SDK includes). Phase 5: Write pytest tests for the keyword matching function covering all edge cases. Pure software maintenance — no hardware required.

items.refined_description: Design three interactive software applications for M5Stack CoreS3 and M5Stack StackChan that demonstrate inter-device communication and sensor integration. The three applications are: (1) Motion Controller — Use CoreS3 BMI270 IMU as a motion controller to control StackChan movements via UART/Bluetooth, with real-time orientation display on CoreS3 screen and corresponding servo/display response on StackChan. (2) Sensor Data Visualizer — CoreS3 reads environmental data (IMU/mic) and streams it to StackChan which visualizes it on its display as waveforms or gauges, demonstrating real-time data pipeline between devices. (3) Interactive Game — A two-player game where CoreS3 serves as controller and StackChan as the game console/graphics renderer, using M5GFX for graphics and GPIO/I2C for communication. Pipeline: embedded-firmware using Arduino framework with M5GFX, M5Unified, and FreeRTOS task management.
